WEEKLY STATUS NOTES - 27 JANUARY

1. CURRENT PROGRESS
The initial phase of the engagement for Brightmoor Renewables is now underway. I have spent the last two days focused on background reading regarding the existing Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) framework. This includes reviewing the historical risk allocation between the generator and the offtaker to ensure our upcoming negotiation strategy aligns with the long-term objectives of the board. The focus remains on securing terms that provide sufficient revenue certainty while maintaining operational flexibility.

2. QUESTIONS FOR COMMERCIAL TEAM
I am preparing a formal list of queries for the Brightmoor Commercial department to clarify internal benchmarks. Key areas of inquiry include:
- Preferred credit support mechanisms and collateral requirements.
- Internal appetite for merchant exposure versus fixed-price volumes.
- Specific reporting requirements for environmental attributes and certificates.
- Desired termination triggers and force majeure definitions.
- Expectations for curtailment compensation clauses.

3. BOARD PAPER DEVELOPMENT
Work has commenced on the draft board paper. The structure will focus on the strategic rationale for the selected PPA structure and how it supports the wider portfolio growth. I am currently outlining the executive summary and the risk-benefit analysis section.

4. CALL LOGISTICS
We need to finalise the schedule for the weekly touchpoint meetings. I suggest a recurring Tuesday morning slot to review progress before the internal Brightmoor management briefing. I will circulate a calendar invitation once the preferred platform is confirmed. Please let me know if there are any specific stakeholders who should be added to the distribution list for these weekly updates.

Hi Maya and Jonas, I hope the week is off to a good start. Just a quick note to keep us on track for the Brightmoor Renewables PPA work. We need to ensure the final board paper is ready by 20 March 2026 to allow for internal review. As you know, the board meets on 24 March, so there is no wiggle room on this one. Let me know if you hit any snags.

Hannah

The national grid operator has unveiled a comprehensive suite of reforms aimed at addressing the backlog within the energy connection queue. Under the new proposals, projects will be required to meet stringent development milestones to maintain their position, moving away from the traditional first-come, first-served model. A spokesperson for the operator, Alistair Vance, stated that the changes are essential to prioritise viable schemes and accelerate the transition to a decarbonised network. Industry analysts suggest the move could significantly reduce waiting times for renewable energy developers.

Brightmoor Renewables has officially completed construction of the Ashby solar farm, marking a significant milestone for the regional energy grid. The facility, which has a capacity of 52 MW, is now fully operational following a successful period of grid synchronisation and safety testing. Project lead Alistair Thorne stated that the site is expected to provide consistent renewable power to thousands of local homes. This development represents a major step in the firm’s commitment to expanding its portfolio of sustainable infrastructure across the country.

A significant technical failure at the GlobalLink card network caused widespread payment disruptions across the region on Wednesday afternoon. The outage, which lasted approximately two hours, prevented thousands of retail transactions and online payments from being processed. Services were restored by early evening following an emergency system reboot. A spokesperson for the network, Alistair Thorne, stated that the issue originated from a routine database update that triggered an unforeseen synchronisation error. Financial institutions are currently monitoring systems for any residual latency as operations return to normal.

Tomás,

I am adding Marcus Vang to this email chain. Marcus has recently joined the compliance team here at Halden Pay and will be representing our internal risk interests as part of the merchant onboarding redesign working group moving forward. 

Please ensure he is included in all future correspondence and calendar invites related to the Northwind Advisory engagement. It would be helpful if everyone could briefly say hello and introduce themselves so he can get up to speed with the various stakeholders involved in the project. 

Marcus, Tomás is our primary contact at Northwind. I will leave you both to coordinate on the outstanding documentation from last week.

Ingrid
Does anyone have a spare laptop charger in the office today? I left mine in the taxi and my battery is already down to ten percent.

The Payment Systems Authority has officially launched a public consultation regarding proposed reductions to existing interchange fee caps. The move follows a comprehensive review of the domestic card market, aimed at assessing whether current limits remain proportionate for merchants and consumers. Regulators are seeking evidence on how a lower ceiling might influence competition and innovation within the financial services sector. "Our objective is to ensure the framework reflects modern transaction volumes," stated agency spokesperson Alistair Thorne. Stakeholders have until the end of the quarter to submit formal responses.

The government has confirmed that the existing sugar levy will be extended to include several new product categories, including sweetened yoghurts and dairy-based snacks. This expansion aims to further incentivise manufacturers to reformulate recipes and reduce overall sugar consumption across the UK. Industry analysts suggest the move could significantly impact supply chains and retail pricing strategies. "This is a decisive step for public health policy," noted Alistair Thorne, a spokesperson for Northwind Advisory. Retailers are now reviewing their inventory to ensure compliance with the updated regulations.

Hi Hannah, hope you had a decent break. I am back at my desk now and getting stuck into the PPA work and the board paper. We should catch up properly soon. Hope the new year is treating you well.

Maya

Dear Hannah,

I hope you had a wonderful break over the festive period and managed to get some well-deserved rest. It has been a rather frantic start to the year here at Kettle & Crumb, as I am sure you can imagine, but we are finally beginning to find our rhythm again.

I was just reflecting on our recent discussions regarding the retail channel strategy and wanted to send a quick note to say hello. It would be lovely to schedule a proper catch up soon to hear how things are progressing on your side and perhaps share a few updates from our end as well.

I look forward to speaking with you properly in the coming weeks.

Best,

Lucy

WEEKLY STATUS NOTES - 11 FEBRUARY

OVERVIEW
The merchant onboarding redesign project for Halden Pay is progressing through the initial design phase. This week focused on refining the user journey for small business applicants and aligning with the technical constraints of the legacy backend.

PORTAL WIREFRAMES
The design team completed the first full walkthrough of the merchant portal wireframes. Feedback from the Halden Pay product owners was generally positive, particularly regarding the simplified document upload process. We have identified a few friction points in the multi-factor authentication flow that require further iteration. The goal is to reduce drop-off rates during the initial sign-up phase without compromising security protocols.

VENDOR DEMOS
We have scheduled a series of demonstrations with third-party identity verification providers. These sessions will allow the team to evaluate how different API integrations might handle automated KYC checks. We are looking for a solution that offers real-time validation to speed up the overall onboarding timeline.

RISK AND COMPLIANCE
Several questions have been drafted for the Risk department. We need clarification on the minimum data requirements for low-risk merchant categories and whether certain manual review steps can be bypassed through enhanced logic. Understanding these parameters is essential before we finalise the automated decisioning engine logic.

NEXT STEPS
Refining the wireframes based on yesterday’s feedback session.
Attending the scheduled vendor presentations to assess technical compatibility.
Meeting with the Risk lead to resolve outstanding compliance queries.
Drafting the functional requirements document for the developer handover.

Hi Sam and Tomás, hope you both had a good start to the week. I’ve just had a nudge from the category manager over at Greenfield Stores regarding our upcoming listing submission. They are pushing for the final margin numbers to be included in the deck before we go to the board. The hard deadline for the full pack is 27 March 2026, so we need to get those figures locked down soon.

Best,

Rohan

KICKOFF MEETING NOTES - 20 JANUARY

ATTENDEES
Sam Reyes (Northwind Advisory), Maya Chen (Brightmoor Renewables), James Thorne (Brightmoor Renewables).

PROJECT OVERVIEW
The primary objective of this engagement is to support Brightmoor Renewables in the finalisation of Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) negotiations and the subsequent drafting of the investment board paper. The focus remains on the Fenmoor wind farm development. Maya confirmed during the session that the project capacity is 180 MW. This figure serves as the baseline for all volume projections and revenue modelling throughout the negotiation phase.

FINANCING REQUIREMENTS
A significant portion of the discussion centred on the conditions precedent set by the project lenders. Ashgrove Bank has been identified as the lead arranger for the debt facility. Their current credit committee requirements stipulate that the project must secure 70% contracted revenue to satisfy debt service coverage ratios before reaching financial close. This threshold is non-negotiable and dictates the minimum volume commitment required from the offtaker.

OFFTAKE STRATEGY
The designated offtaker for the Fenmoor project is Tarn Valley Utilities. Initial terms have been exchanged, but Northwind Advisory is tasked with reviewing the price floor mechanisms and curtailment clauses to ensure they align with the bankability requirements mentioned above. The board paper must clearly articulate how the Tarn Valley Utilities contract mitigates long-term merchant power price exposure.

DELIVERABLES AND TIMELINE
1. PPA Clause Review: Northwind to provide a redline of the current draft focusing on force majeure and termination payments.
2. Financial Modelling: Integration of the 180 MW production estimates into the revenue stack.
3. Board Paper: A comprehensive briefing document for the Brightmoor Renewables executive team, detailing the risk-adjusted returns and the status of the Ashgrove Bank facility.

COMMUNICATION PLAN
To maintain momentum and ensure all workstreams remain aligned with the 70% hedging target, the team will hold weekly Thursday calls. These sessions will serve as the primary forum for updates on the Tarn Valley Utilities negotiations and any technical adjustments to the Fenmoor site layout. Sam Reyes will circulate the agenda twenty-four hours in advance of each call.
Ingrid, do you have an ETA for that risk-scoring matrix you mentioned earlier? I need to review the logic before we present the redesign to the Halden Pay team tomorrow morning.

Hi Sam,

Thanks for sending over the revised term sheet. I have had a quick look through the numbers with the internal team this morning. We are happy to accept the 12 year duration as proposed, but the 74/MWh floor is still causing some friction. It is currently sitting above the 71/MWh limit that finance originally signed off on, so we have a bit of a gap to bridge there.

Could you please provide a reworked sensitivity table reflecting these levels before we circulate the board pre-read? On another note, I know I promised you the grid-connection study last week. Apologies for the delay on that, things have been a bit hectic here and it is slipping slightly. I will get it across to you by 6 March at the latest.

Maya

Hi Sam, I’ve been thinking more about the scale of our ambition for the retail channel strategy. Right now we are sitting at 640 stockists, which feels like a solid foundation, but I really want us to push the boundaries over the next eighteen months. The goal is to hit 1,200 stores by the end of 2026. It sounds like a massive leap, I know, but with the right distribution partners I’m convinced we can get there. Let’s make sure the upcoming deck reflects this level of growth.

Kettle & Crumb - Statement of Work: retail channel strategy
Author: Priya Nair
Date: Monday 12 January 2026

1. OVERVIEW
This Statement of Work outlines the professional services to be provided by Northwind Advisory to Kettle & Crumb. The primary objective of this engagement is to develop a comprehensive retail channel strategy to support the expansion of the client’s biscuit and snack bar portfolio across major UK grocery and convenience outlets.

2. SCOPE OF SERVICES
Northwind Advisory will conduct a detailed analysis of the current consumer snack landscape to identify growth opportunities. The consultancy will provide strategic guidance on positioning Kettle & Crumb products within competitive retail environments, ensuring alignment with brand values and production capabilities.

3. DELIVERABLES
The engagement will result in the following formal outputs:
- Retail channel strategy: A roadmap identifying priority retailers, geographic focus areas, and distribution timelines.
- Retailer margin model: A dynamic financial framework designed to calculate sustainable pricing structures and trade discounts for various retail partners.
- Promotions plan: A structured calendar of promotional activities and seasonal campaigns intended to drive volume and brand awareness at the point of sale.

4. PROJECT TIMELINE
The duration of this engagement is fixed at three months, commencing immediately upon the formal signing of this document.

5. FEES AND PAYMENT TERMS
The services described herein are provided on a fixed-term basis. Kettle & Crumb agrees to a monthly retainer of £12,000 for the duration of the project. This results in a total professional fee of £36,000 for the full three-month term. 

Invoices will be issued at the start of each month of service. All fees are exclusive of VAT and any pre-approved out-of-pocket expenses incurred during the delivery of the project.

6. CONFIDENTIALITY
Both Northwind Advisory and Kettle & Crumb agree to maintain the confidentiality of all proprietary data, financial models, and strategic plans shared during this engagement. No information regarding the retail channel strategy shall be disclosed to third parties without prior written consent.

Global commodity markets are reacting to unprecedented volatility as cocoa prices hit a record high this week. Analysts suggest that supply chain constraints in West Africa, combined with shifting weather patterns, have tightened global stocks to critical levels. This surge is expected to place significant pressure on confectionery manufacturers and boutique chocolatiers alike. "We are monitoring the situation closely as input costs rise across the sector," noted Julian Vane, a spokesperson for Northwind Advisory. Industry experts predict that retail price adjustments may be inevitable by next quarter.

PROPOSAL: PPA NEGOTIATION STRATEGY FOR BRIGHTMOOR RENEWABLES
Authored by: Hannah Voss
Date: Thursday 11 December 2025

1. OBJECTIVE
Northwind Advisory is pleased to submit this proposal to support Brightmoor Renewables in securing an optimal long-term agreement for the Fenmoor wind farm. Our primary focus is to provide strategic commercial oversight during the final stages of discussions with the counterparty, Tarn Valley Utilities. We aim to ensure that the commercial terms reflect current market benchmarks while mitigating long-term volume and price risks.

2. SCOPE OF WORK: PPA NEGOTIATION
Northwind will act as the lead commercial advisor for the PPA negotiation process. This includes a comprehensive review of the current term sheet offered by Tarn Valley Utilities to identify areas for value enhancement. We will focus on balancing the fixed-price components against market-indexed variables to protect project returns. Our team will participate in direct sessions with the offtaker to resolve outstanding clauses related to curtailment compensation, negative pricing protection, and credit support requirements.

3. SCOPE OF WORK: BOARD PAPER
Following the conclusion of the negotiation phase, Northwind will draft a formal board paper for the Brightmoor Renewables executive team. This document will provide a detailed summary of the negotiated PPA, a risk-benefit analysis of the chosen offtake structure, and a clear recommendation for execution. The paper will be designed to provide the board with the necessary confidence that the agreement supports the project’s debt-sizing requirements and overall financial stability.

4. METHODOLOGY
Our approach is data-driven and collaborative. We will begin with a baseline assessment of the Fenmoor wind farm’s projected output against the specific requirements of the offtaker. Throughout the engagement, we will maintain a continuous feedback loop with the Brightmoor internal legal and finance teams to ensure all technical specifications are aligned with the commercial strategy.

5. DELIVERABLES
The engagement will conclude with the delivery of the finalised PPA term sheet and the comprehensive board paper. Northwind Advisory remains committed to delivering these outputs within the agreed project timeline to facilitate a timely financial close for the Fenmoor asset.

WEEKLY STATUS NOTES - 24 FEBRUARY

1. PROMOTION PLAN STRUCTURE
The draft framework for the retail promotion plan is now under review. We have shifted the focus towards high-traffic seasonal windows to ensure maximum visibility for the new biscuit range. The current structure prioritises end-of-aisle placements and multi-buy incentives across the major supermarket accounts. We are waiting for the internal sales team to confirm which specific product lines will be included in the initial push before we finalise the tactical calendar.

2. PACKAGING QUESTIONS
Several queries have arisen regarding the secondary packaging for the snack bar multipacks. There is a concern that the current cardboard specifications may not withstand the pressure of automated shelf-stacking systems used by certain retailers. We need to clarify if the branding on the outer cases aligns with the updated visual identity guidelines. Additionally, we are investigating whether the sustainable materials mandate will impact the lead times for the bespoke display units.

3. MEETING LOGISTICS
The steering committee meeting originally planned for the end of the week will be moved to a virtual format to accommodate travel schedules. A revised invitation will be circulated shortly. We also need to schedule a separate technical deep-dive with the logistics lead to discuss pallet configurations. Please ensure all relevant stakeholders have access to the shared folder containing the latest strategy decks. We will use the standard dial-in details for all upcoming touchpoints unless otherwise notified.

HALDEN PAY - STATEMENT OF WORK: MERCHANT ONBOARDING REDESIGN

1. OVERVIEW
This Statement of Work (SOW) defines the professional services to be provided by Northwind Advisory to Halden Pay. The primary objective of this engagement is to modernise the merchant onboarding experience to reduce friction while maintaining rigorous compliance standards. Priya Nair will serve as the lead consultant for the duration of this project.

2. SCOPE OF SERVICES
The consultancy services shall encompass the following core workstreams:

A. ONBOARDING FLOW REDESIGN
Northwind Advisory will conduct a comprehensive audit of the current merchant application journey. We will deliver a streamlined, mobile-responsive onboarding flow redesign aimed at increasing conversion rates and reducing manual intervention.

B. RISK-SCORING REVIEW
A detailed evaluation of the existing automated risk-scoring logic will be performed. This includes refining the parameters for instant approvals and identifying high-risk triggers that require manual underwriting, ensuring alignment with current fintech regulatory expectations.

C. PORTAL REQUIREMENTS
We will define the functional and technical requirements for the updated merchant portal. This includes documentation for self-service features, status tracking, and identity verification integration points.

3. PROJECT TIMELINE
The engagement will commence immediately upon execution of this SOW. The target go-live for the new onboarding flow is 14 April 2026. Both parties agree to adhere to a structured project plan to meet this milestone.

4. FEES AND PAYMENT TERMS
This engagement is undertaken on a fixed-fee basis. The total professional fee for the defined scope is £62,000. This amount is payable in three instalments according to the following schedule:

- Initial instalment: £22,000 due upon project commencement.
- Interim instalment: £20,000 due upon delivery of the risk-scoring review.
- Final instalment: £20,000 due upon completion of the portal requirements documentation.

5. CHANGE MANAGEMENT
Any deviations from the scope defined in this document must be formally documented. All change requests need written approval from the CFO of Halden Pay before any additional work is undertaken or costs are incurred.

6. AUTHORISATION
Authored by Priya Nair on Friday 12 December 2025.

The Treasury has confirmed that stringent new regulations for buy-now-pay-later providers will come into force early next year. The framework aims to bring interest-free credit products under the supervision of the Financial Conduct Authority, requiring lenders to perform mandatory affordability checks. Industry analysts suggest the move will provide greater protection for consumers against spiralling debt. "These measures ensure the sector operates with the same transparency as traditional lending," noted Alistair Vance, a spokesperson for the Regulatory Oversight Committee. Providers must now prepare for increased compliance reporting.

Dublin-based fintech firm Halden Pay has officially introduced instant payout capabilities for its merchant network across Ireland, effective 24 February. PROPOSAL: MERCHANT ONBOARDING REDESIGN FOR HALDEN PAY

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Halden Pay currently faces significant friction within its merchant acquisition funnel. Internal data indicates that 31% of prospective merchants drop out during the initial application process. This attrition represents a substantial loss in potential transaction volume and market share. Northwind Advisory proposes a comprehensive redesign of the onboarding journey to reduce complexity while maintaining rigorous compliance standards.

2. PROBLEM STATEMENT
The existing onboarding process is hindered by redundant data requests and a fragmented user interface. Merchants frequently abandon the process when faced with manual document uploads that lack real-time validation. This high abandonment rate suggests that the current workflow does not align with the expectations of modern small-to-medium enterprises seeking rapid payment integration.

3. PROPOSED APPROACH
Our strategy focuses on three core pillars to streamline the merchant experience:

SIMPLIFIED KYC FLOW
We will restructure the Know Your Customer (KYC) requirements to follow a progressive disclosure model. By integrating third-party data verification services, we can pre-populate fields and reduce the manual burden on the applicant.

RISK-BASED SCORING
Northwind will design a dynamic risk engine that categorises applicants based on industry and volume projections. Low-risk merchants will benefit from an accelerated "fast-track" approval path, while enhanced due diligence is reserved for high-risk profiles.

SELF-SERVE PORTAL
A new, mobile-responsive portal will provide merchants with a clear checklist of their application status. This transparency reduces the volume of support enquiries and allows applicants to resume saved sessions across different devices.

4. PROJECT PHASES

PHASE I: DISCOVERY AND AUDIT
Review of current technical architecture and stakeholder interviews to identify specific friction points.

PHASE II: DESIGN AND PROTOTYPING
Creation of high-fidelity wireframes for the new portal and mapping the logic for the automated risk engine.

PHASE III: IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT
Collaborating with the Halden Pay engineering team to oversee the integration of new API endpoints and validation logic.

PHASE IV: TESTING AND OPTIMISATION
Conducting user acceptance testing and refining the flow based on initial conversion metrics.

PPA GLOSSARY AND BACKGROUND

This document provides a plain-language overview of common terminology used in Power Purchase Agreement negotiations. These definitions serve as a baseline for the upcoming board paper and internal strategy sessions.

1. FLOOR PRICE
The minimum guaranteed price per megawatt-hour that the generator will receive. If market prices drop below this level, the off-taker pays the difference. This provides the project with the revenue certainty required for debt financing.

2. TERM
The duration of the contract. In renewable energy, this typically spans ten to fifteen years. The length of the term is critical for matching the project’s lifecycle and ensuring long-term investment stability.

3. INDEXATION
A mechanism used to adjust the strike price over time, usually linked to inflation measures like the Consumer Price Index. This ensures the real value of the revenue stream is maintained against rising operational costs.

4. CURTAILMENT
Occurs when the grid operator or off-taker restricts the delivery of energy to the grid, often due to oversupply or network constraints. PPA negotiations focus on who bears the financial risk of lost production during these periods.

5. BASELOAD SHAPE
A delivery profile where the generator commits to providing a constant, steady volume of electricity regardless of actual wind or solar conditions. This often requires the generator to purchase top-up power from the market if their own assets are under-producing, introducing significant volume risk compared to a pay-as-produced structure.

RETAILER LANDSCAPE WORKING DRAFT

1. LARGE MULTIPLE SUPERMARKETS
The major grocery chains remain the primary volume drivers for the consumer snacks category. These retailers operate on a centralised buying model where category managers oversee specific segments such as sweet biscuits or healthy bars. Decisions are driven by shelf-space productivity and promotional cycles. For a brand like Kettle & Crumb, entry requires a robust supply chain and the ability to support national marketing campaigns. Listing fees and margin expectations are high, but the reach is unparalleled.

2. CONVENIENCE AND FORECOURTS
This channel focuses on immediate consumption and impulse purchases. Buying is often fragmented, split between head office listings for managed estates and independent wholesalers for franchised sites. Product format is critical here; single-serve bars perform better than multi-pack biscuits. Range reviews are frequent, and retailers prioritise high-rotation stock due to limited shelf capacity.

3. DISCOUNTERS
The discounter model relies on a limited assortment strategy and high volume. They typically favour private label products but increasingly use established brands to drive footfall. Buying teams are lean and negotiations focus heavily on net-net pricing. To succeed in this space, a supplier must demonstrate extreme cost efficiency and the ability to provide exclusive pack sizes or temporary promotional lines.

4. SPECIALIST AND PREMIUM RETAIL
High-end delis and health-focused chains offer a platform for brand building and premium positioning. Buying is often decentralised or managed by boutique distributors. While volumes are lower, these retailers allow for higher price points and direct engagement with a health-conscious demographic.
